```{r knitr-options, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      comment = "#>", fig.align = "center")
```

**This analysis is exploratory.** It was specified on 9 October 2026, after
every registered result of the five studies was known. No registration, the
plan of analysis filed for a study before its results were seen, names it,
and nothing in it changes a registered verdict. Every table it writes says
so in its last column, `analysis_status`, and each figure says so at its foot.
Every justification was written after its rating, so nothing here is evidence
of why anyone rated as they did. The analysis describes what people wrote once
their number was chosen.

# 0. What this file does

In Studies 2, 4 and 5 each participant was told that the artist Alex made a
first artwork either with design software and sketching tools (Human) or by
prompting an AI system (AI). Each then rated second works that Alex made by
hand from it, at three levels of modification: None (the first work shown
again unchanged), Slight (colour and contrast adjustments) and Dramatic
(substantial changes by hand). After every rating the participant wrote a
short justification.

Each study's own files already looked for topics in those justifications in
two steps. A topic model, fitted without the label, gave each response a
weight on each topic, and the label's effect on each weight was then tested
topic by topic, as if the weights were measured without error. That approach
stays as each study registered it.

This file asks the same kind of question with the label inside the topic
model, on the three studies pooled. A structural topic model, fitted with the
R package stm, finds topics, groups of words that tend to appear in the same
responses, and lets the share of each topic in a response, its prevalence,
depend on covariates, quantities recorded for each response. Here the
covariates are the source label, the modification level, the rating and the
study. The label's effect on each topic is then estimated from repeated draws
of every response's topic shares, so its uncertainty includes the uncertainty
of those shares. It does not include the uncertainty of the topics' word
lists, which are held at their estimates; section 7 examines that uncertainty
separately.

The question is whether the label changes what people write about, and
whether that change differs as the second work moves away from the first. For
each topic the file gives the AI minus Human difference in the topic's
expected share at each level, the difference averaged over the levels, and
the change in the difference from None to Dramatic.

No person and no language model labels, codes or judges any response, and no
topic is named by anyone. Each topic is identified by its number, its
highest-probability words and its most distinctive words, all computed by the
model.

This file:

1. reads each study's long data file, its word counts and the wording of its
   rated items, and checks each against the record of the run that wrote it
   (section 2);
2. removes the words that the task itself put in front of every participant,
   and the words too rare to model (section 3);
3. builds one corpus, a collection of responses, for each question, with its
   covariates (section 4);
4. chooses the number of topics for each question by a rule fixed in code
   (section 5);
5. fits the model at that number, lists each topic's words and example
   identifiers, and checks how stable the topics are (sections 6 and 7);
6. estimates the label's effect on each topic (section 8) and draws one
   figure per question (section 9);
7. records the status of every fit, says what the numbers show, and records
   the run (sections 10 to 12).

Creativity is the primary question, because it is the one question asked of
original artworks and second works alike. Transformativeness and essence
change are secondary.

Eight limits apply throughout.

- Every justification was written after its rating. The words describe what
  people wrote once they had rated, not what made them rate as they did.
- The responses are short. After the vocabulary rule a modelled response
  holds a few words (section 4 gives the numbers), so each response's topic
  shares rest on little evidence, and the model leans on its covariates and
  on the other responses to estimate them.
- A response that keeps no word after the vocabulary rule is dropped, and
  at None the share dropped differs between the labels (section 4 gives the
  shares). Every label effect is therefore an effect among the responses
  that kept a word, and part of a difference at None may come from which
  responses kept one rather than from what the kept ones say.
- Each participant wrote many responses, but the model treats every response
  as independent of the others. stm has no term for the participant, so the
  intervals of section 8 do not widen for responses that share a writer, and
  they are likely too narrow.
- The effects rest on 25 simulated sets of topic shares, stm's default, so
  every standard error carries simulation noise, and another seed would move
  each interval somewhat.
- The model lets each study have its own baseline share of each topic but
  assumes the label's effect is the same in all three studies. It leaves out
  Study 4's source time and Study 5's editing time.
- The item wording differs between studies. Study 2's creativity and essence
  items carried no definition, while Studies 4 and 5 used Study 1's. The
  vocabulary rule removes each study's own item words, so a word such as
  *original* is removed from the responses of Studies 4 and 5 and kept in
  those of Study 2. Section 3 lists every such word.
- The topics a model finds depend in part on where its search starts.
  Section 7 measures how far they do here, and a label effect on a topic that
  another start does not recover says less than one on a topic that it does.

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# dplyr, tidyr, tibble and readr build and write the tables. stm fits the
# structural topic models. MASS draws from the normal distributions of the
# effect estimates. parallel runs the model fits on several processor cores.
# ggplot2 draws the figures and knitr prints the tables.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(readr)
  library(stm)
  library(MASS, include.only = "mvrnorm")
  library(ggplot2)
})
```

## 1.2 Paths and constants

```{r paths}
# Every path is found from this file's own folder, which is the working
# directory when the file is knitted. These environment variables override
# the defaults:
#   STRUCTURAL_TOPICS_DIR            this folder, where the outputs go
#   PIPELINE_DIR                     the analysis pipeline folder, two levels up
#   STUDY_SHARED_R                   the folder of the shared R helpers
#   STUDY_SHARED_PYTHON              the folder of the shared Python module
#   STUDY2_DIR, STUDY4_DIR, STUDY5_DIR  the three study folders
# Printed paths are relative to the pipeline folder, so no printed line names
# a folder particular to one machine.
HERE <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("STRUCTURAL_TOPICS_DIR", getwd()), mustWork = TRUE)
PIPELINE_DIR <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("PIPELINE_DIR", file.path(HERE, "..", "..")),
                              mustWork = TRUE)
SHARED_R      <- Sys.getenv("STUDY_SHARED_R", file.path(PIPELINE_DIR, "shared", "R"))
SHARED_PYTHON <- Sys.getenv("STUDY_SHARED_PYTHON", file.path(PIPELINE_DIR, "shared", "python"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "fit_status.R"))
show <- function(p) relative_path(p, PIPELINE_DIR)

STUDIES <- c("Study 2", "Study 4", "Study 5")
STUDY_DIRS <- setNames(vapply(c(2, 4, 5), function(n) {
  normalizePath(Sys.getenv(paste0("STUDY", n, "_DIR"),
                           file.path(PIPELINE_DIR, paste("Study", n))), mustWork = TRUE)
}, character(1)), STUDIES)

TABLES  <- file.path(HERE, "tables")
FIGURES <- file.path(HERE, "figures")
for (p in c(TABLES, FIGURES)) dir.create(p, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Each study's files. Studies 2 and 5 hold the Human or AI label in the column
# source, and Study 4 in the column label, where source names the source
# image. The word counts name the second work stimulus_id, and the long data
# files name it work_id.
STUDY_FILES <- tibble(study = STUDIES, n = c(2, 4, 5),
                      label_column = c("source", "label", "source")) %>%
  mutate(folder         = STUDY_DIRS[study],
         long           = file.path(folder, paste0("study", n, "_long_with_text.csv")),
         wordcounts     = file.path(folder, "nlp", paste0("study", n, "_text_wordcounts.csv")),
         item_scales    = file.path(folder, "tables", paste0("study", n, "_item_scales.csv")),
         quant_manifest = file.path(folder, "tables", paste0("study", n, "_quant_run_manifest.csv")),
         quant_inputs   = file.path(folder, "tables", paste0("study", n, "_quant_run_inputs.csv")),
         text_manifest  = file.path(folder, "tables", paste0("study", n, "_text_run_manifest.csv")))

INPUTS <- c(
  shared_text_module = file.path(SHARED_PYTHON, "study_text.py"),
  unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(STUDY_FILES)), function(k) {
    s <- STUDY_FILES[k, ]
    tag <- paste0("study", s$n)
    setNames(c(s$long, s$wordcounts, s$item_scales, s$quant_manifest, s$text_manifest),
             paste0(tag, c("_long", "_wordcounts", "_item_scales", "_quant_manifest",
                           "_text_manifest")))
  })),
  study5_quant_inputs = STUDY_FILES$quant_inputs[STUDY_FILES$study == "Study 5"])
missing_inputs <- names(INPUTS)[!file.exists(INPUTS)]
if (length(missing_inputs) > 0) {
  stop("Missing input(s): ", paste(missing_inputs, collapse = ", "),
       ". Run each study's pipeline on its real labels first.")
}
for (p in names(INPUTS)) cat(sprintf("%-22s %s\n", p, show(INPUTS[[p]])))
cat("Tables to:  ", show(TABLES), "\nFigures to: ", show(FIGURES), "\n")

# The constants of the analysis. The seed is the one the registrations name
# for R. A seed is the number that starts a random-number generator, so that
# a rerun draws the same numbers.
SEED            <- 20260421L
K_RANGE         <- 4:12
MIN_RESPONSES   <- 5L
STABILITY_SEEDS <- SEED + 0:4
N_SIMS          <- 25L    # estimateEffect's default number of simulated topic shares
N_DRAWS         <- 500L   # draws per simulation, as stm's summary of the effects uses
TOP_WORDS       <- 7L
LABEL_WORDS     <- 4L
N_EXAMPLES      <- 3L
ALPHA           <- 0.05
QUESTIONS  <- c("creativity", "transformativeness", "essence_change")
ROLE       <- c(creativity = "primary", transformativeness = "secondary",
                essence_change = "secondary")
QUESTION_LABELS <- c(creativity = "Creativity", transformativeness = "Transformativeness",
                     essence_change = "Essence change")
SOURCE_LEVELS <- c("Human", "AI")
MOD_LEVELS    <- c("None", "Slight", "Dramatic")
REGISTERED <- tibble(study = STUDIES, participants = c(235L, 117L, 223L),
                     analysed_ratings = c(20659L, 6178L, 11768L),
                     six_point_ratings = c(0L, 140L, 274L))
ANALYSIS_STATUS <- paste("exploratory; specified on 9 October 2026, after every registered",
                         "result was known; no registration names it; changes no",
                         "registered verdict")
CAPTION_LEAD <- paste("Exploratory, specified after every registered result was known;",
                      "changes no registered verdict.")

# The prevalence model: the expected share of each topic in a response
# depends on the label, the level, the two together, the centred rating and
# the study. The model has no content covariate, so each topic has one list
# of word probabilities for every response.
PREVALENCE_TEXT <- "~ source * modification + rating_c + study"
PREVALENCE      <- as.formula(PREVALENCE_TEXT)

# The model fits run on several processor cores where the platform allows
# it: one on Windows, where R cannot copy a running session to other cores,
# and otherwise one fewer than the machine has, up to nine. Every fit gives
# the same result from the same seed, so the results do not depend on the
# number of cores.
N_CORES <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") 1L else
  max(1L, min(9L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L))
cat("Processor cores used for the fits:", N_CORES, "\n")

# Progress lines go to the console that runs the knit, with the clock time,
# so a long run can be followed while it works.
progress <- function(...) {
  cat(format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), "|", ..., "\n", file = stderr())
}
progress("Structural topics: setup done")
```

## 1.3 Run record and table helpers

```{r run-record}
# The run record stores the SHA-256 checksum of every input (a 64-character
# fingerprint of the file's exact bytes), deletes the previous run's manifest
# now and each output's previous copy before the chunk that writes it, and
# writes the manifest last. A manifest on disk therefore means the run
# reached its end.
run <- start_run_record(INPUTS, file.path(TABLES, "structural_topics_run_manifest.csv"), HERE)
run$inputs <- run$inputs %>% mutate(file = show(INPUTS))
cat("Run identifier:", run$run_id, "\n")

# Every table carries the analysis status in its last column, so a table read
# on its own still says what it is.
table_path <- function(name) file.path(TABLES, name)
write_table <- function(df, name) {
  write_csv(mutate(df, analysis_status = ANALYSIS_STATUS), table_path(name), na = "NA")
}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("structural_topics_run_inputs.csv"))
write_table(run$inputs, "structural_topics_run_inputs.csv")

# Every table printed in this report opens its caption with the same status.
show_table <- function(df, caption, digits = 3) {
  knitr::kable(df, digits = digits, caption = paste(CAPTION_LEAD, caption))
}
```

# 2. Inputs and checks

## 2.1 Reading the inputs

Each long data file holds one row per participant, second work and question,
with the label, the level, the rating, the justification and `label_mode`,
which says whether the labels are real or shuffled. Each word-count file holds
one row per response and word, with the word's count in that response. The
shared text module made it: it lower-cased each justification, split it into
words, removed the function words (words such as *the* and *of* that carry
grammar rather than content), and kept the words used in at least two
responses of the study. The item-scale table holds the stem and the answer
labels of every rated item.

```{r read-inputs}
# Every column is read as text, with no value read as missing, as the text
# notebooks read the long data files; the rating and the number of answer
# options are then turned into numbers.
read_text_table <- function(path) {
  read_csv(path, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character(),
           progress = FALSE)
}
long <- setNames(lapply(STUDY_FILES$long, function(p) {
  read_text_table(p) %>% mutate(rating = as.numeric(rating), k_points = as.integer(k_points))
}), STUDIES)
wordcounts <- setNames(lapply(STUDY_FILES$wordcounts, function(p) {
  read_text_table(p) %>% mutate(count = as.integer(count))
}), STUDIES)
item_scales <- setNames(lapply(STUDY_FILES$item_scales, read_text_table), STUDIES)
for (s in STUDIES) {
  cat(sprintf("%s: %d rows of long data, %d word-count rows, %d rated items\n",
              s, nrow(long[[s]]), nrow(wordcounts[[s]]), nrow(item_scales[[s]])))
}
progress("Inputs read")
```

## 2.2 The checks

The run stops unless every input is the file its study's real run wrote and
reproduces the study's registered analysed sample. A run manifest is the
record a study's run writes last, listing every file it wrote with its
checksum. A blind run, one on shuffled labels, writes its records to a
`blind_run/` folder, so a match with the manifest in a study's `tables/`
folder can only come from a real run.

- The long data file and the item-scale table of Studies 2 and 4 must match
  the study's quantitative run manifest. Study 5's item-scale table is
  written by its build script and read by its quantitative run, which records
  its checksum among that run's inputs; it must match that record.
- The word counts must match the study's text run manifest. The text notebook
  reads no label and no rating, so it has no real or blind mode.
- `label_mode` must say `real` on every row, and the participants, analysed
  ratings and six-point ratings must equal the registered counts.
- Every response in the word counts must be a response in the long data file,
  and no function word may appear in them.
- The word pattern and function words read from the shared module (section
  2.3), applied in R to every justification, must reproduce the deposited word
  counts exactly. This shows that the item wording of section 3 is split into
  words by the same rule as the responses.

```{r input-checks}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("structural_topics_input_checks.csv"))

sha <- function(path) unname(tools::sha256sum(path))
listed_sha <- function(manifest_path, file_label, column = "file") {
  m <- read_csv(manifest_path, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                progress = FALSE)
  row <- m[m[[column]] == file_label, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(row) != 1) return(NA_character_)
  if ("written_this_run" %in% names(row) && !identical(row$written_this_run, "TRUE")) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  row$sha256
}
check <- function(study, quantity, expected, observed) {
  tibble(study = study, quantity = quantity,
         expected = as.character(expected), observed = as.character(observed),
         pass = identical(as.character(expected), as.character(observed)))
}
input_checks <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(STUDY_FILES)), function(k) {
  s <- STUDY_FILES[k, ]
  d <- long[[s$study]]
  w <- wordcounts[[s$study]]
  reg <- REGISTERED[REGISTERED$study == s$study, ]
  scales_listed <- if (s$study == "Study 5") {
    listed_sha(s$quant_inputs, basename(s$item_scales))
  } else {
    listed_sha(s$quant_manifest, file.path("tables", basename(s$item_scales)))
  }
  long_keys <- paste(d$id, d$work_id, d$dimension, sep = "|")
  wc_keys   <- unique(paste(w$id, w$stimulus_id, w$dimension, sep = "|"))
  bind_rows(
    check(s$study, "long data file equals the one listed in the real run manifest",
          TRUE, identical(sha(s$long), listed_sha(s$quant_manifest, basename(s$long)))),
    check(s$study, "item-scale table equals the one the real quantitative run recorded",
          TRUE, identical(sha(s$item_scales), scales_listed)),
    check(s$study, "word counts equal the ones listed in the text run manifest",
          TRUE, identical(sha(s$wordcounts),
                          listed_sha(s$text_manifest, file.path("nlp", basename(s$wordcounts))))),
    check(s$study, "label_mode says real on every row", TRUE,
          "label_mode" %in% names(d) && all(d$label_mode == "real")),
    check(s$study, "participants", reg$participants, n_distinct(d$id)),
    check(s$study, "analysed ratings, on the five-point items", reg$analysed_ratings,
          sum(d$k_points == 5)),
    check(s$study, "six-point ratings, left out", reg$six_point_ratings,
          sum(d$k_points == 6)),
    check(s$study, "one row per participant, second work and question", TRUE,
          !anyDuplicated(long_keys)),
    check(s$study, "every response in the word counts is a response in the long data file",
          TRUE, all(wc_keys %in% long_keys)),
    check(s$study, "labels are Human or AI on every row", TRUE,
          all(d[[s$label_column]] %in% SOURCE_LEVELS)),
    check(s$study, "levels are None, Slight or Dramatic on every row", TRUE,
          all(d$modification %in% MOD_LEVELS)),
    check(s$study, "questions are the three rated ones on every row", TRUE,
          all(d$dimension %in% QUESTIONS)))
}))
```

## 2.3 The shared word lists, read from the shared module

The function words, the task vocabulary and the pattern that splits a text
into words are read from the shared Python module, `shared/python/study_text.py`,
so this file applies the lists the studies applied and keeps no copy of its
own. The task vocabulary is the shared list of words that the Study 1
instrument put in front of every participant, such as *alex*, *artwork* and
*creativity*. The module removes them, with their plurals, before its own
topic model.

```{r shared-lists}
py_text <- paste(readLines(INPUTS[["shared_text_module"]], warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
extract_one <- function(pattern, what) {
  m <- regmatches(py_text, gregexpr(pattern, py_text, perl = TRUE))[[1]]
  if (length(m) != 1) stop("Could not read ", what, " from the shared text module.")
  m
}
fw_block <- extract_one('FUNCTION_WORDS = sorted\\(set\\("""[^"]*"""', "the function words")
FUNCTION_WORDS <- sort(unique(strsplit(trimws(
  gsub('^FUNCTION_WORDS = sorted\\(set\\("""|"""$', "", fw_block)), "\\s+")[[1]]))
tv_block <- extract_one('TASK_VOCABULARY = \\[[^\\]]*\\]', "the task vocabulary")
TASK_VOCABULARY <- gsub('"', "", regmatches(tv_block, gregexpr('"[^"]+"', tv_block))[[1]])
wr_block <- extract_one('WORD_RE = re\\.compile\\(r"[^"]*"\\)', "the word pattern")
WORD_PATTERN <- sub('^WORD_RE = re\\.compile\\(r"', "", sub('"\\)$', "", wr_block))
# The module's own test of a task word: the word itself or its plural in s.
plural_rule <- grepl('return word in TASK_VOCABULARY or (word.endswith("s") and word[:-1] in TASK_VOCABULARY)',
                     py_text, fixed = TRUE)
stopifnot(plural_rule, identical(WORD_PATTERN, "[a-z][a-z']+"))
cat("Function words:", length(FUNCTION_WORDS), "| task words:", length(TASK_VOCABULARY),
    "| word pattern:", WORD_PATTERN, "\n")
cat("Task vocabulary:", paste(TASK_VOCABULARY, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# The shared tokenize(): lower-case the text, take every run of letters and
# apostrophes of two characters or more that starts with a letter, and drop
# the function words.
tokenize <- function(text) {
  lowered <- tolower(text)
  words <- regmatches(lowered, gregexpr(WORD_PATTERN, lowered, perl = TRUE))
  lapply(words, function(w) w[!w %in% FUNCTION_WORDS])
}
is_task_word <- function(word) {
  word %in% TASK_VOCABULARY |
    (endsWith(word, "s") & substr(word, 1, nchar(word) - 1) %in% TASK_VOCABULARY)
}

# The R tokenizer, applied to every justification, must give the deposited
# word counts: each response's count of each word used in at least two
# responses of its study.
recount_check <- bind_rows(lapply(STUDIES, function(s) {
  d <- long[[s]]
  toks <- tokenize(d$response_text)
  rc <- tibble(id = rep(d$id, lengths(toks)), stimulus_id = rep(d$work_id, lengths(toks)),
               dimension = rep(d$dimension, lengths(toks)), word = unlist(toks)) %>%
    count(id, stimulus_id, dimension, word, name = "count")
  kept <- rc %>% count(word, name = "responses") %>% filter(responses >= 2) %>% pull(word)
  rc <- rc %>% filter(word %in% kept) %>% arrange(id, stimulus_id, dimension, word)
  dep <- wordcounts[[s]] %>% arrange(id, stimulus_id, dimension, word)
  bind_rows(
    check(s, "the R tokenizer reproduces the deposited word counts", TRUE,
          isTRUE(all.equal(as.data.frame(rc), as.data.frame(dep), check.attributes = FALSE))),
    check(s, "no function word in the word counts", TRUE,
          !any(wordcounts[[s]]$word %in% FUNCTION_WORDS)))
}))
input_checks <- bind_rows(input_checks, recount_check)
write_table(input_checks, "structural_topics_input_checks.csv")
show_table(input_checks, "Table 2.1. Every input check. The run stops if any fails.")
if (!all(input_checks$pass)) stop("An input disagrees with its study's record or registered sample.")
progress("Input checks passed")
```

# 3. The vocabulary rule

A word that every participant read appears wherever people restate the
question. Left in, such words would form topics about the wording of the
task rather than about what people said of the work. The rule, fixed in code,
removes from each study's responses:

- the shared task vocabulary, with the plural of each task word, as the
  shared module removes it;
- every word in the stems or the answer labels of that study's rated items,
  read from `tables/studyN_item_scales.csv` and split into words by the same
  shared rule. The table holds every rated item, the two six-point
  transformativeness items included, since participants read those too.

Then, within each question's corpus, the three studies pooled, the rule keeps
only words used in at least 5 responses. A word used more rarely carries too
little information to place in a topic.

```{r item-words}
# Each study's item words: every word of every stem and answer label, split by
# the shared rule. The answer labels of one item are joined by " | " in the
# table, and the bar is not a letter, so it splits them.
item_words <- setNames(lapply(STUDIES, function(s) {
  sc <- item_scales[[s]]
  sort(unique(unlist(tokenize(c(sc$stem, sc$anchors)))))
}), STUDIES)
for (s in STUDIES) {
  cat(sprintf("%s, %d item words: %s\n", s, length(item_words[[s]]),
              paste(item_words[[s]], collapse = ", ")))
}
only_some <- setdiff(Reduce(union, item_words), Reduce(intersect, item_words))
cat("Item words of some studies but not all:", paste(only_some, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r apply-vocabulary}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("structural_topics_vocabulary_removed.csv"),
                  table_path("structural_topics_corpus_counts.csv"))

# The analysed responses: the five-point items only, as each study's primary
# analysis keeps them, with the label, level, rating and study.
responses <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(STUDY_FILES)), function(k) {
  s <- STUDY_FILES[k, ]
  long[[s$study]] %>%
    filter(k_points == 5) %>%
    transmute(study = s$study, id, work = work_id, question = dimension,
              source = .data[[s$label_column]], modification, rating)
}))
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(table(factor(responses$study, levels = STUDIES))),
                    REGISTERED$analysed_ratings))

# The word counts of the analysed responses only.
words_all <- bind_rows(lapply(STUDIES, function(s) {
  wordcounts[[s]] %>% transmute(study = s, id, work = stimulus_id, question = dimension,
                                word, count)
})) %>%
  semi_join(responses, by = c("study", "id", "work", "question"))

# The removal rule for each study: the task words with their plurals, and the
# study's item words. The plurals are those found among the words of any of
# the three studies, so the task part of the rule is the same in every study.
present <- unique(words_all$word)
plurals <- sort(present[is_task_word(present) & !present %in% TASK_VOCABULARY])
rule_words <- bind_rows(lapply(STUDIES, function(s) {
  bind_rows(
    tibble(study = s, word = TASK_VOCABULARY, reason = "task vocabulary"),
    tibble(study = s, word = plurals, reason = "plural of a task word"),
    tibble(study = s, word = setdiff(item_words[[s]], c(TASK_VOCABULARY, plurals)),
           reason = "item wording"))
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(rule_words[c("study", "word")]))

# Each removed word, with the number of analysed responses to each question
# in that study that used it. A word of the rule that no response used has 0.
use_by_study <- words_all %>% count(study, question, word, name = "responses_using_it")
# A word in the rule of every study is removed from all responses alike; any
# other is removed from some studies' responses and kept in the others'.
in_every_rule <- Reduce(intersect, split(rule_words$word, rule_words$study))
vocab_removed_rule <- rule_words %>%
  tidyr::crossing(question = QUESTIONS) %>%
  left_join(use_by_study, by = c("study", "question", "word")) %>%
  mutate(responses_using_it = coalesce(responses_using_it, 0L),
         removed_in_all_three_studies = word %in% in_every_rule)

words_rule <- words_all %>%
  anti_join(rule_words, by = c("study", "word"))

# The rarity rule, within each question's pooled corpus.
responses_per_word <- words_rule %>% count(question, word, name = "responses_using_it")
rare <- responses_per_word %>% filter(responses_using_it < MIN_RESPONSES)
words_kept <- words_rule %>% anti_join(rare, by = c("question", "word"))

vocab_removed <- bind_rows(
  vocab_removed_rule %>%
    transmute(question, scope = study, word, reason, responses_using_it,
              removed_in_all_three_studies),
  rare %>% transmute(question, scope = "three studies pooled", word,
                     reason = paste("used in fewer than", MIN_RESPONSES, "responses"),
                     responses_using_it, removed_in_all_three_studies = NA)) %>%
  mutate(question = factor(question, levels = QUESTIONS)) %>%
  arrange(question, scope, reason, desc(responses_using_it), word) %>%
  mutate(question = as.character(question))
write_table(vocab_removed, "structural_topics_vocabulary_removed.csv")

# The removed task and item words that responses used, with how often, for
# the report.
removed_used <- vocab_removed_rule %>%
  group_by(study, word, reason) %>%
  summarise(responses_using_it = sum(responses_using_it), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(responses_using_it > 0) %>%
  arrange(study, desc(responses_using_it))
show_table(removed_used %>%
             group_by(study, reason) %>%
             summarise(words = paste0(word, " (", responses_using_it, ")", collapse = ", "),
                       .groups = "drop"),
           paste("Table 3.1. Task and item words removed from each study's responses,",
                 "with the number of analysed responses, over the three questions,",
                 "that used each. Words of the rule that no response used are in the",
                 "deposited table only."))
rare_summary <- rare %>% group_by(question) %>%
  summarise(rare_words = n(), responses_using_them = sum(responses_using_it), .groups = "drop")
show_table(rare_summary, paste("Table 3.2. Words removed for being used in fewer than",
                               MIN_RESPONSES, "responses to the question."))
```

# 4. The corpora and the covariates

For each question one corpus pools the analysed responses of the three
studies. A response that keeps no word after the vocabulary rule has nothing
for a topic model to read, so it is dropped and counted. Each kept response is
a document of the model, with four covariates:

- `source`, the label, Human or AI;
- `modification`, the level, None, Slight or Dramatic;
- `rating_c`, the rating minus the mean rating of the question's modelled
  responses, so that a value of 0 is an average rating. The rating is in the
  model so that a label effect on a topic is not merely the label's effect on
  the rating carried over into the words.
- `study`, Study 2, 4 or 5, which gives each study its own baseline share of
  each topic.

R's default coding of factors (treatment contrasts, which compare each level
with the first) is used; section 8 computes every difference from the model's
predictions for each cell, so the coding does not change any reported number.

```{r corpora}
# One corpus per question. A document is a two-row matrix, as stm requires:
# the first row holds the indices of the response's words in the
# question's vocabulary, sorted, and the second row their counts.
build_corpus <- function(q) {
  w <- words_kept %>% filter(question == q)
  vocab <- sort(unique(w$word), method = "radix")
  meta <- responses %>% filter(question == q) %>%
    semi_join(w, by = c("study", "id", "work")) %>%
    arrange(study, id, work)
  meta <- meta %>%
    mutate(doc_key = paste(study, id, work, sep = "|"),
           source = factor(source, levels = SOURCE_LEVELS),
           modification = factor(modification, levels = MOD_LEVELS),
           study = factor(study, levels = STUDIES),
           rating_c = rating - mean(rating))
  by_doc <- split(w, paste(w$study, w$id, w$work, sep = "|"))[meta$doc_key]
  documents <- lapply(by_doc, function(x) {
    ix <- match(x$word, vocab)
    o <- order(ix)
    rbind(as.integer(ix[o]), as.integer(x$count[o]))
  })
  names(documents) <- NULL
  stopifnot(length(documents) == nrow(meta), all(vapply(documents, ncol, integer(1)) > 0))
  list(question = q, documents = documents, vocab = vocab, meta = as.data.frame(meta),
       rating_mean = mean(meta$rating))
}
corpora <- setNames(lapply(QUESTIONS, build_corpus), QUESTIONS)

# The counts at each step, by question and study, and pooled.
count_step <- function(q, s) {
  r <- responses %>% filter(question == q, study %in% s)
  a <- words_all %>% filter(question == q, study %in% s)
  b <- words_rule %>% filter(question == q, study %in% s)
  k <- words_kept %>% filter(question == q, study %in% s)
  m <- corpora[[q]]$meta %>% filter(study %in% s)
  doc_len <- vapply(corpora[[q]]$documents[corpora[[q]]$meta$study %in% s],
                    function(d) sum(d[2, ]), numeric(1))
  tibble(question = q, scope = if (length(s) == 1) s else "three studies pooled",
         analysed_responses = nrow(r),
         responses_with_a_counted_word = n_distinct(paste(a$study, a$id, a$work)),
         responses_after_task_and_item_rule = n_distinct(paste(b$study, b$id, b$work)),
         modelled_responses = nrow(m),
         dropped_no_counted_word = nrow(r) - nrow(m),
         modelled_human = sum(m$source == "Human"), modelled_ai = sum(m$source == "AI"),
         modelled_none = sum(m$modification == "None"),
         modelled_slight = sum(m$modification == "Slight"),
         modelled_dramatic = sum(m$modification == "Dramatic"),
         participants_modelled = n_distinct(paste(m$study, m$id)),
         word_tokens_counted = sum(a$count), word_tokens_after_task_and_item_rule = sum(b$count),
         word_tokens_modelled = sum(k$count),
         vocabulary_size = if (length(s) == 1) n_distinct(k$word) else length(corpora[[q]]$vocab),
         mean_words_per_modelled_response = mean(doc_len),
         median_words_per_modelled_response = median(doc_len),
         rating_mean_of_question = corpora[[q]]$rating_mean)
}
corpus_counts <- bind_rows(lapply(QUESTIONS, function(q) {
  bind_rows(lapply(STUDIES, function(s) count_step(q, s)), count_step(q, STUDIES))
}))
stopifnot(all(corpus_counts$analysed_responses == corpus_counts$modelled_responses +
                corpus_counts$dropped_no_counted_word))
write_table(corpus_counts, "structural_topics_corpus_counts.csv")
show_table(corpus_counts %>%
             select(question, scope, analysed_responses, dropped_no_counted_word,
                    modelled_responses, modelled_human, modelled_ai, vocabulary_size,
                    word_tokens_modelled, mean_words_per_modelled_response),
           "Table 4.1. The corpus of each question, by study and pooled.", digits = 2)
progress("Corpora built:", paste(sprintf("%s %d documents, %d words", QUESTIONS,
                                         vapply(corpora, function(x) length(x$documents), integer(1)),
                                         vapply(corpora, function(x) length(x$vocab), integer(1))),
                                 collapse = "; "))
```

The model reads only the responses that kept a word, so a label effect
compares the responses that kept one in the AI arm, the participants told
that the first work was made by prompting an AI system, with those in the
Human arm. Table 4.2 gives the share of analysed responses dropped in each
cell of label and level. Where the two labels lose different shares at a
level, the responses the model compares at that level were selected
differently in the two arms.

```{r dropped-by-cell}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("structural_topics_dropped_by_label_and_level.csv"))
# Each analysed response is marked modelled or dropped, and the dropped share
# is counted in each cell of label and level, by study and pooled.
SCOPES <- c(STUDIES, "three studies pooled")
dropped_by_cell <- bind_rows(lapply(QUESTIONS, function(q) {
  kept <- corpora[[q]]$meta %>%
    transmute(study = as.character(study), id, work, modelled = TRUE)
  d <- responses %>% filter(question == q) %>%
    left_join(kept, by = c("study", "id", "work")) %>%
    mutate(modelled = coalesce(modelled, FALSE))
  bind_rows(d, mutate(d, study = "three studies pooled")) %>%
    group_by(question, scope = study, source, modification) %>%
    summarise(analysed_responses = n(), dropped_no_counted_word = sum(!modelled),
              share_dropped = mean(!modelled), .groups = "drop")
})) %>%
  mutate(question = factor(question, levels = QUESTIONS), scope = factor(scope, levels = SCOPES),
         source = factor(source, levels = SOURCE_LEVELS),
         modification = factor(modification, levels = MOD_LEVELS)) %>%
  arrange(question, scope, modification, source) %>%
  mutate(across(c(question, scope, source, modification), as.character))
# The cells add up to the counts of Table 4.1.
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
  as.data.frame(dropped_by_cell %>% group_by(question, scope) %>%
    summarise(a = as.numeric(sum(analysed_responses)),
              d = as.numeric(sum(dropped_no_counted_word)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(question, scope)),
  as.data.frame(corpus_counts %>% arrange(question, scope) %>%
    transmute(question, scope, a = as.numeric(analysed_responses),
              d = as.numeric(dropped_no_counted_word))),
  check.attributes = FALSE)))
write_table(dropped_by_cell, "structural_topics_dropped_by_label_and_level.csv")
show_table(dropped_by_cell %>% filter(scope == "three studies pooled") %>%
             select(question, modification, source, analysed_responses,
                    dropped_no_counted_word, share_dropped),
           paste("Table 4.2. Analysed responses dropped for keeping no word, by label and",
                 "level, the three studies pooled. The deposited table gives each study."))
```

# 5. Choosing the number of topics

The number of topics, K, is chosen by a rule fixed in code. `stm::searchK`
fits the model at every K from 4 to 12. Before it fits, it draws a random
tenth of the documents, from seed 20260421, sets aside half the word
occurrences of each drawn document (rounded down, and at least one), and fits
each model without them. A drawn document with only one distinct word gives
up none, so fewer documents than a tenth lose words; Table 5.1 gives both
numbers. The held-out likelihood is the log probability that a fitted model
gives to each word it did not see, averaged over the set-aside words of each
document and then over the documents; a higher value means the model predicts
unseen words better. The chosen K is the one with the highest held-out
likelihood, and an exact tie goes to the smaller K.

Two further measures are reported for every K, from the same fits. Semantic
coherence is high when a topic's most probable words tend to appear in the
same documents. Exclusivity is high when a topic's top words are probable in
that topic and rare in the others. searchK computes both on each topic's ten
most probable words and averages them over topics; exclusivity uses FREX with
weight 0.7, a score that combines how frequent a word is in the topic with how
exclusive it is to it.

Every fit starts from a spectral initialisation, a starting point computed
from the matrix of how often each pair of words appears together, with no
random draw, so the same data always give the same start. A fit is an
iterative search, the expectation-maximisation algorithm, which alternates
between estimating each response's topic shares and estimating the topics
and covariate effects. It stops when the bound, the quantity the search
maximises, rises by less than 0.00001 of itself from one iteration to the
next, or falls; stm allows at most 500 iterations. A fit that reached 500 is
marked as not settled.

```{r search-k}
search_results <- list()
for (q in QUESTIONS) {
  cp <- corpora[[q]]
  progress(sprintf("searchK for %s: K = %d to %d on %d documents and %d words, %d cores",
                   q, min(K_RANGE), max(K_RANGE), length(cp$documents), length(cp$vocab),
                   min(N_CORES, length(K_RANGE))))
  started <- Sys.time()
  sk <- stm::searchK(cp$documents, cp$vocab, K = K_RANGE, init.type = "Spectral",
                     heldout.seed = SEED, cores = min(N_CORES, length(K_RANGE)),
                     prevalence = PREVALENCE, data = cp$meta, seed = SEED, verbose = FALSE)
  minutes <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), started, units = "mins"))
  progress(sprintf("searchK for %s done in %.1f minutes", q, minutes))
  # searchK's own call to make.heldout, repeated with the same seed, counts
  # the drawn documents that gave up words; it skips a drawn document with
  # one distinct word.
  held <- stm::make.heldout(cp$documents, cp$vocab, N = floor(0.1 * length(cp$documents)),
                            proportion = 0.5, seed = SEED)
  search_results[[q]] <- as_tibble(lapply(sk$results, unlist)) %>%
    transmute(question = q, role = ROLE[[q]], K = as.integer(K),
              heldout_likelihood = heldout, semantic_coherence = semcoh,
              exclusivity = exclus, residual_dispersion = residual,
              lower_bound = bound, em_iterations = as.integer(em.its),
              reached_iteration_limit = em_iterations >= 500L,
              heldout_documents_drawn = floor(0.1 * length(cp$documents)),
              heldout_documents_with_words_held_out = length(held$missing$index),
              heldout_share_of_words = 0.5, heldout_seed = SEED,
              minutes_for_all_k = minutes)
}
```

```{r choose-k}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("structural_topics_searchk.csv"),
                  table_path("structural_topics_chosen_k.csv"))
searchk <- bind_rows(search_results)

# The rule: the highest held-out likelihood, an exact tie going to the
# smaller K. Ordering by the held-out likelihood, largest first, and then by
# K puts the chosen K first and the runner-up second.
chosen_k <- searchk %>%
  group_by(question, role) %>%
  summarise(chosen_K = K[order(-heldout_likelihood, K)][1],
            heldout_likelihood_chosen = heldout_likelihood[order(-heldout_likelihood, K)][1],
            runner_up_K = K[order(-heldout_likelihood, K)][2],
            heldout_likelihood_runner_up = heldout_likelihood[order(-heldout_likelihood, K)][2],
            rule = paste("highest held-out likelihood over K =", min(K_RANGE), "to",
                         paste0(max(K_RANGE), "; an exact tie goes to the smaller K")),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(question = factor(question, levels = QUESTIONS)) %>% arrange(question) %>%
  mutate(question = as.character(question))
searchk <- searchk %>% left_join(chosen_k %>% select(question, chosen_K), by = "question") %>%
  mutate(chosen = K == chosen_K) %>% select(-chosen_K)
write_table(searchk, "structural_topics_searchk.csv")
write_table(chosen_k, "structural_topics_chosen_k.csv")
show_table(searchk %>% select(question, K, heldout_documents_drawn,
                              heldout_documents_with_words_held_out, heldout_likelihood,
                              semantic_coherence, exclusivity, em_iterations, chosen),
           "Table 5.1. The searchK diagnostics for every K.", digits = 4)
show_table(chosen_k %>% select(-rule), "Table 5.2. The chosen K of each question.", digits = 4)
```

```{r search-k-figure, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
# The three diagnostics against K, one row of panels per question, with the
# chosen K marked by a filled point.
searchk %>%
  select(question, K, chosen, `Held-out likelihood` = heldout_likelihood,
         `Semantic coherence` = semantic_coherence, Exclusivity = exclusivity) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(`Held-out likelihood`, `Semantic coherence`, Exclusivity),
               names_to = "diagnostic", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(question = factor(QUESTION_LABELS[question], levels = QUESTION_LABELS),
         diagnostic = factor(diagnostic, levels = c("Held-out likelihood",
                                                    "Semantic coherence", "Exclusivity"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(K, value)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(fill = chosen), shape = 21, size = 2, colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "white", `TRUE` = "black"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = K_RANGE) +
  facet_grid(diagnostic ~ question, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Number of topics, K", y = NULL,
       caption = paste(CAPTION_LEAD, "The filled point is the chosen K.")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = "grey60"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey30"))
```

# 6. The models at the chosen number of topics

## 6.1 The fits

For each question the model is fitted once more, at the chosen K, to every
modelled document, from the spectral start and with seed 20260421. The same K
is also fitted five more times from a different start, for the stability
check of section 7: the latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) start, which draws
initial topics by a short run of a simpler topic model and so depends on the
seed, here 20260421 to 20260425. The eighteen fits run on several processor
cores at once. Section 10 gives the convergence of each; section 8 says what
follows for a question whose spectral fit did not converge.

```{r final-fits}
# Fit one model and keep every warning it raises, its error if it stops, and
# how long it took.
fit_stm <- function(q, K, init, seed) {
  cp <- corpora[[q]]
  warns <- character(0)
  started <- Sys.time()
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(stm::stm(cp$documents, cp$vocab, K = K, prevalence = PREVALENCE,
                      data = cp$meta, init.type = init, seed = seed, verbose = FALSE),
             error = function(e) e),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  list(question = q, K = K, init = init, seed = seed, fit = fit, warnings = warns,
       minutes = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), started, units = "mins")))
}
jobs <- bind_rows(lapply(QUESTIONS, function(q) {
  K <- chosen_k$chosen_K[chosen_k$question == q]
  bind_rows(tibble(question = q, K = K, init = "Spectral", seed = SEED),
            tibble(question = q, K = K, init = "LDA", seed = STABILITY_SEEDS))
}))
progress(sprintf("Fitting %d models at the chosen K on %d cores", nrow(jobs), N_CORES))
started <- Sys.time()
fits <- if (N_CORES > 1L) {
  parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(jobs)), function(i) {
    fit_stm(jobs$question[i], jobs$K[i], jobs$init[i], jobs$seed[i])
  }, mc.cores = N_CORES, mc.preschedule = FALSE)
} else {
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(jobs)), function(i) {
    fit_stm(jobs$question[i], jobs$K[i], jobs$init[i], jobs$seed[i])
  })
}
failed <- vapply(fits, function(f) inherits(f, "try-error") || inherits(f$fit, "error"),
                 logical(1))
if (any(failed)) stop("A model fit at the chosen K stopped with an error.")
progress(sprintf("Fits at the chosen K done in %.1f minutes",
                 as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), started, units = "mins"))))

spectral <- setNames(lapply(QUESTIONS, function(q) {
  fits[[which(jobs$question == q & jobs$init == "Spectral")]]$fit
}), QUESTIONS)
# The search stops when the bound, the quantity the search maximises, rises
# by less than a set share of itself from one iteration to the next, or
# falls. The last relative change shows how far a fit that reached the limit
# was from that threshold.
relative_change <- function(bound) {
  n <- length(bound)
  if (n < 2) return(NA_real_)
  (bound[n] - bound[n - 1]) / abs(bound[n - 1])
}
fit_rows <- bind_rows(lapply(fits, function(f) {
  tibble(question = f$question, model = paste0("stm, ", f$init, " start"),
         K = f$K, seed = f$seed, documents = length(corpora[[f$question]]$documents),
         fit_error = FALSE, converged = isTRUE(f$fit$convergence$converged),
         em_iterations = length(f$fit$convergence$bound),
         final_lower_bound = tail(f$fit$convergence$bound, 1),
         last_relative_change = relative_change(f$fit$convergence$bound),
         convergence_threshold = f$fit$settings$convergence$em.converge.thresh,
         minutes = f$minutes, messages = paste(unique(f$warnings), collapse = " | "))
}))
print(as.data.frame(fit_rows %>% select(question, model, K, seed, converged, em_iterations,
                                        last_relative_change)))
```

## 6.2 The words of each topic

Each topic is a probability distribution over the question's vocabulary.
Its highest-probability words are the seven it gives the most probability
to. Its FREX words are the seven with the highest FREX score, which combines
a word's rank by how often the topic uses it with its rank by how exclusive
it is to the topic, here with equal weight, so a FREX word is both common in
the topic and rare in the others. Each topic's mean share is its expected
proportion averaged over the question's documents.

```{r topic-words}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("structural_topics_topic_words.csv"),
                  table_path("structural_topics_topic_examples.csv"))
topic_words <- bind_rows(lapply(QUESTIONS, function(q) {
  fit <- spectral[[q]]
  lt <- stm::labelTopics(fit, n = TOP_WORDS)
  K <- fit$settings$dim$K
  tibble(question = q, role = ROLE[[q]], topic = seq_len(K),
         topic_label = vapply(seq_len(K), function(k) {
           paste0("Topic ", k, ": ", paste(lt$prob[k, seq_len(LABEL_WORDS)], collapse = ", "))
         }, character(1)),
         highest_probability_words = apply(lt$prob, 1, paste, collapse = ", "),
         frex_words = apply(lt$frex, 1, paste, collapse = ", "),
         mean_topic_share = colMeans(fit$theta))
}))
write_table(topic_words, "structural_topics_topic_words.csv")
show_table(topic_words %>% select(question, topic, highest_probability_words, frex_words,
                                  mean_topic_share),
           "Table 6.1. The seven highest-probability and seven FREX words of every topic.")
```

## 6.3 Example identifiers

For each topic, the three documents with the largest share of that topic are
listed by their study, participant identifier and second work, so that a
reader can find them in the deposited data. No response text is printed. An
exact tie in the share goes to the document that comes first in the order of
study, participant and second work.

```{r topic-examples}
topic_examples <- bind_rows(lapply(QUESTIONS, function(q) {
  fit <- spectral[[q]]
  meta <- corpora[[q]]$meta
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(fit$settings$dim$K), function(k) {
    top <- order(-fit$theta[, k], seq_len(nrow(meta)))[seq_len(N_EXAMPLES)]
    tibble(question = q, topic = k, example = seq_len(N_EXAMPLES),
           study = as.character(meta$study[top]), id = meta$id[top], work = meta$work[top],
           topic_share = fit$theta[top, k])
  }))
}))
write_table(topic_examples, "structural_topics_topic_examples.csv")
show_table(topic_examples, "Table 6.2. Three example identifiers for every topic.")
```

# 7. Stability

A topic found from one start might not be found from another. Each LDA refit
of section 6.1 is compared with the spectral fit: for each spectral topic, the
correlation (Pearson's, across the vocabulary) between its word probabilities
and those of every topic of the refit, and the largest of these, the
best-match correlation. A value near 1 means some topic of the refit puts
nearly the same probabilities on the same words. The table gives the mean of
the five best-match correlations for each topic, the smallest of them, and in
how many refits the best match of the topic is also the best match of another
spectral topic, which would mean the refit merged them.

```{r stability}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("structural_topics_stability.csv"))
word_probs <- function(fit) exp(fit$beta$logbeta[[1]])
stability <- bind_rows(lapply(QUESTIONS, function(q) {
  ref <- word_probs(spectral[[q]])
  per_seed <- bind_rows(lapply(which(jobs$question == q & jobs$init == "LDA"), function(i) {
    r <- cor(t(ref), t(word_probs(fits[[i]]$fit)))
    best <- apply(r, 1, which.max)
    tibble(topic = seq_len(nrow(r)), seed = jobs$seed[i],
           best_match_correlation = apply(r, 1, max), best_match = best,
           shared = best %in% best[duplicated(best)],
           refit_converged = isTRUE(fits[[i]]$fit$convergence$converged))
  }))
  per_seed %>% group_by(topic) %>%
    summarise(mean_best_match_correlation = mean(best_match_correlation),
              min_best_match_correlation = min(best_match_correlation),
              refits_with_best_match_shared = sum(shared),
              refits = n(), refits_converged = sum(refit_converged), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(question = q, role = ROLE[[q]], .before = 1) %>%
    mutate(seeds = paste(range(STABILITY_SEEDS), collapse = " to "),
           start_compared = "LDA start against the spectral fit")
})) %>%
  left_join(topic_words %>% select(question, topic, topic_label), by = c("question", "topic")) %>%
  relocate(topic_label, .after = topic)
write_table(stability, "structural_topics_stability.csv")
show_table(stability %>% select(question, topic_label, mean_best_match_correlation,
                                min_best_match_correlation, refits_with_best_match_shared),
           "Table 7.1. Best-match correlations of the five LDA refits with the spectral fit.")
progress("Stability done")
```

# 8. The label's effect on each topic

## 8.1 The method

`stm::estimateEffect` fits a linear regression of each topic's share on the
covariates of the prevalence model. A document's topic shares are estimates,
not data, so it uses the method of composition: it draws a full set of
document shares from the fitted model 25 times, fits the regression to each
draw, and keeps each fit's coefficients with their covariance matrix, which
holds each coefficient's squared standard error and how each pair of
coefficients varies together. The draws use stm's "Global" approximation to
the uncertainty of the shares, which centres each document's draw on its
estimated shares and gives every document the same spread, estimated once
from the whole model. The variation from draw to draw carries the
uncertainty of each document's topic shares into the effects. The topics'
word probabilities are held at their estimates, so their uncertainty is not
carried; section 7 examines it separately.

For each topic, each of the 25 coefficient sets gives 500 draws from a normal
distribution with its coefficients as the mean and its covariance matrix, as
stm's own summary of the effects does, 12,500 draws in all. Each draw gives
the predicted share of the topic in each of the six cells of label and level,
at the average rating and in the same study; with no label by study or label
by rating term in the model, a difference between cells is the same in every
study and at every rating. Three quantities follow:

a. the AI minus Human difference in expected topic share at None, at Slight
   and at Dramatic;
b. the AI minus Human difference averaged over the three levels with equal
   weight;
c. whether the label difference changes across the levels: the difference at
   Dramatic minus the difference at None.

The estimate is the mean of the draws, its standard error their standard
deviation, and its t statistic the estimate divided by the standard error.
The 95 percent interval is the estimate plus or minus the standard error
times the 97.5th percentile of the t distribution, the distribution that the
t statistic follows when the true difference is zero, here with the residual
degrees of freedom of the regression (documents minus coefficients). The
two-sided p-value, the probability of a t statistic at least as far from zero
if the true difference were zero, comes from the same distribution, as in
stm's summary. The Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, which controls the expected share of false
findings among the results called significant, is applied across the topics
of each question, separately for (b) and for (c). It is description: no
p-value here tests a registered hypothesis, and the (a) values carry no
adjustment.

The pipeline's rule for a model that did not converge, written in
`shared/R/fit_status.R` for the mixed models and applied in the same way
here, is that its numbers carry no interval, p-value or verdict. When the
spectral fit of a question did not converge (section 6.1), its estimates are
kept as description, and its standard errors, intervals, t statistics and
p-values are set to missing, with a note saying why.

```{r effects}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("structural_topics_label_effects_by_level.csv"),
                  table_path("structural_topics_label_effects_averaged_and_change.csv"))

# The predicted cells: the six cells of label and level, at rating_c = 0 and
# in Study 2. Each cell's row of the design matrix holds the covariate values
# that multiply the coefficients, so the row times the coefficients is the
# cell's predicted share. Each reported quantity is a difference of rows.
cells <- expand.grid(source = factor(SOURCE_LEVELS, levels = SOURCE_LEVELS),
                     modification = factor(MOD_LEVELS, levels = MOD_LEVELS))
cells$rating_c <- 0
cells$study <- factor(STUDIES[1], levels = STUDIES)
X_cells <- model.matrix(PREVALENCE, data = cells)
rownames(X_cells) <- paste(cells$source, cells$modification)
diff_at <- function(level) X_cells[paste("AI", level), ] - X_cells[paste("Human", level), ]
L_level <- rbind(None = diff_at("None"), Slight = diff_at("Slight"),
                 Dramatic = diff_at("Dramatic"))
L_all <- rbind(L_level,
               `averaged over levels` = colMeans(L_level),
               `Dramatic minus None` = L_level["Dramatic", ] - L_level["None", ])
# Under R's default coding the difference at None is the AI coefficient, the
# difference at Slight adds the AI by Slight coefficient, and the change from
# None to Dramatic is the AI by Dramatic coefficient. The check confirms that
# the differences built from the cells say the same.
unit <- function(...) {
  v <- setNames(numeric(ncol(X_cells)), colnames(X_cells))
  v[c(...)] <- 1
  v
}
stopifnot(all.equal(L_all["None", ], unit("sourceAI")),
          all.equal(L_all["Slight", ], unit("sourceAI", "sourceAI:modificationSlight")),
          all.equal(L_all["Dramatic minus None", ], unit("sourceAI:modificationDramatic")))

effect_rows <- list()
effect_status <- list()
for (q in QUESTIONS) {
  fit <- spectral[[q]]
  K <- fit$settings$dim$K
  meta <- corpora[[q]]$meta
  warns <- character(0)
  set.seed(SEED)
  eff <- withCallingHandlers(
    stm::estimateEffect(as.formula(paste0("1:", K, " ", PREVALENCE_TEXT)), fit,
                        metadata = meta, uncertainty = "Global", nsims = N_SIMS),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  stopifnot(identical(names(eff$parameters[[1]][[1]]$est), colnames(X_cells)))
  rdf <- nrow(meta) - ncol(X_cells)
  converged <- isTRUE(fit$convergence$converged)
  set.seed(SEED)
  for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    draws <- do.call(rbind, lapply(eff$parameters[[k]], function(p) {
      mvrnorm(N_DRAWS, p$est, p$vcov)
    }))
    contrast <- draws %*% t(L_all)
    est <- colMeans(contrast)
    se  <- apply(contrast, 2, sd)
    tval <- est / se
    effect_rows[[length(effect_rows) + 1]] <- tibble(
      question = q, role = ROLE[[q]], topic = k, quantity = rownames(L_all),
      estimate = est, se = se,
      ci95_lo = est - qt(0.975, rdf) * se, ci95_hi = est + qt(0.975, rdf) * se,
      t = tval, df = rdf, p = 2 * pt(abs(tval), rdf, lower.tail = FALSE),
      draws = nrow(draws), model_converged = converged)
  }
  effect_status[[q]] <- tibble(question = q, model = "estimateEffect, Global uncertainty",
                               K = K, seed = SEED, documents = nrow(meta), fit_error = FALSE,
                               converged = NA, em_iterations = NA_integer_,
                               final_lower_bound = NA_real_, last_relative_change = NA_real_,
                               convergence_threshold = NA_real_, minutes = NA_real_,
                               messages = paste(unique(warns), collapse = " | "))
  progress(sprintf("Effects for %s done", q))
}
# A question whose model did not converge keeps its estimates as description;
# every uncertainty column is set to missing and the note says why.
UNCERTAINTY_COLUMNS <- c("se", "ci95_lo", "ci95_hi", "t", "p")
effects <- bind_rows(effect_rows) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(UNCERTAINTY_COLUMNS), ~ ifelse(model_converged, .x, NA_real_)),
         note = ifelse(model_converged, "",
                       paste("the model fit did not converge within 500 iterations, so the",
                             "interval and p-value are set to NA; the estimate is description"))) %>%
  left_join(topic_words %>% select(question, topic, topic_label), by = c("question", "topic")) %>%
  relocate(topic_label, .after = topic) %>%
  mutate(difference = "AI minus Human, expected topic share",
         nsims = N_SIMS, draws_per_sim = N_DRAWS, uncertainty = "Global")

by_level <- effects %>% filter(quantity %in% MOD_LEVELS) %>%
  rename(level = quantity) %>%
  mutate(adjustment = "none; description")
avg_change <- effects %>% filter(!quantity %in% MOD_LEVELS) %>%
  group_by(question, quantity) %>%
  mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
         adjustment = "Benjamini-Hochberg across the topics of this question; description") %>%
  ungroup()
cat("Questions whose model did not converge, reported as description only:",
    if (all(effects$model_converged)) "none" else
      paste(unique(effects$question[!effects$model_converged]), collapse = ", "), "\n")
write_table(by_level, "structural_topics_label_effects_by_level.csv")
write_table(avg_change, "structural_topics_label_effects_averaged_and_change.csv")
```

## 8.2 The difference at each level

```{r effects-by-level-table}
show_table(by_level %>% select(question, topic_label, level, estimate, ci95_lo, ci95_hi, p),
           "Table 8.1. AI minus Human in expected topic share at each level, uncorrected.",
           digits = 4)
```

## 8.3 The difference averaged over levels, and its change

```{r effects-avg-table}
show_table(avg_change %>% select(question, topic_label, quantity, estimate, ci95_lo, ci95_hi,
                                 p, p_bh),
           paste("Table 8.2. AI minus Human averaged over levels, and the difference at",
                 "Dramatic minus the difference at None, with Benjamini-Hochberg",
                 "adjusted p-values as description."), digits = 4)
```

# 9. The figures

One greyscale figure per question shows each topic's AI minus Human difference
in expected share at None, Slight and Dramatic, with its 95 percent interval.
Each topic is labelled by its number and its four highest-probability words. A
point to the right of the dashed line means AI-arm responses gave the topic a
larger share. The intervals carry no adjustment for the number of topics.

```{r figures, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 6}
fig_paths <- unlist(lapply(QUESTIONS, function(q) {
  file.path(FIGURES, paste0("structural_topics_", q, c(".pdf", ".png")))
}))
run_clear_outputs(run, fig_paths)

LEVEL_SHAPES <- c(None = 21, Slight = 22, Dramatic = 24)
LEVEL_FILLS  <- c(None = "white", Slight = "grey60", Dramatic = "black")
LEVEL_OFFSET <- c(None = 0.22, Slight = 0, Dramatic = -0.22)
FIG_STATUS <- paste("Exploratory analysis, specified after every registered result was",
                    "known; it changes no registered verdict. Intervals are 95 percent and",
                    "unadjusted; responses that share a writer are treated as independent.")
figure_for <- function(q) {
  converged <- all(by_level$model_converged[by_level$question == q])
  status <- if (converged) FIG_STATUS else paste(
    FIG_STATUS, "This model did not converge within 500 iterations, so its estimates",
    "are description and no interval is drawn.")
  d <- by_level %>% filter(question == q) %>%
    mutate(level = factor(level, levels = MOD_LEVELS),
           y = -topic + LEVEL_OFFSET[as.character(level)])
  K <- max(d$topic)
  labels <- topic_words %>% filter(question == q) %>% arrange(topic)
  ggplot(d, aes(x = estimate, y = y)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = ci95_lo, xmax = ci95_hi), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4,
                   na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = level, fill = level), size = 2, colour = "black") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = LEVEL_SHAPES, name = "Modification level") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = LEVEL_FILLS, name = "Modification level") +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = -seq_len(K), labels = labels$topic_label, expand = c(0.03, 0.03)) +
    labs(x = "AI minus Human, expected topic share", y = NULL,
         title = paste0(QUESTION_LABELS[[q]], " (", ROLE[[q]], "): the label's effect on each topic"),
         caption = paste(strwrap(status, 110), collapse = "\n")) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
          plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey30", size = 8),
          plot.caption.position = "plot",
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3))
}
for (q in QUESTIONS) {
  K <- max(by_level$topic[by_level$question == q])
  height <- 1.8 + 0.42 * K
  g <- figure_for(q)
  ggsave(file.path(FIGURES, paste0("structural_topics_", q, ".pdf")), g,
         width = 7.5, height = height, device = "pdf")
  ggsave(file.path(FIGURES, paste0("structural_topics_", q, ".png")), g,
         width = 7.5, height = height, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  print(g)
}
```

# 10. Fit status

A model fit converged when the expectation-maximisation search stopped
because the bound, the quantity it maximises, rose by less than 0.00001 of
itself from one iteration to the next, or fell, before the limit of 500
iterations. For each fit at the chosen K the table gives that last relative
change. searchK does not return the convergence flag, so its fits are marked
by whether they reached the limit. The effects come from linear regressions,
which have no iterative search, and the table records any warning they
raised.

```{r fit-status}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("structural_topics_fit_status.csv"))
fit_status <- bind_rows(
  searchk %>% transmute(question, model = "searchK, Spectral start, held-out documents",
                        K, seed = SEED, documents = NA_integer_, fit_error = FALSE,
                        converged = !reached_iteration_limit, em_iterations,
                        final_lower_bound = lower_bound, last_relative_change = NA_real_,
                        convergence_threshold = NA_real_, minutes = NA_real_, messages = ""),
  fit_rows %>% mutate(documents = as.integer(documents)),
  bind_rows(effect_status) %>% mutate(documents = as.integer(documents))) %>%
  mutate(question = factor(question, levels = QUESTIONS)) %>%
  arrange(question) %>% mutate(question = as.character(question))
write_table(fit_status, "structural_topics_fit_status.csv")
show_table(fit_status %>% count(model, converged, name = "fits"),
           "Table 10.1. Fits by kind and convergence.")
cat("Fits:", nrow(fit_status), "| topic-model fits that did not settle:",
    sum(fit_status$converged %in% FALSE), "| fits with a warning:",
    sum(nzchar(fit_status$messages)), "\n")
```

# 11. What the numbers show

```{r summary-text, results = "asis"}
# Every number in this section is read from the tables above.
f3 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
f4 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 4)
pct <- function(x) formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = 1)
n_ <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
p_text <- function(p) if (p < 1e-4) "below .0001" else paste("=", signif(p, 2))
trend_text <- function(h) {
  steps <- sign(diff(h))
  if (all(steps > 0)) "rising with every added topic"
  else if (all(steps < 0)) "falling with every added topic"
  else sprintf("rising at %d of the %d steps from one K to the next and falling at the others",
               sum(steps > 0), length(steps))
}
words_of <- function(q, k) {
  topic_words$highest_probability_words[topic_words$question == q & topic_words$topic == k]
}
for (q in QUESTIONS) {
  ck <- chosen_k %>% filter(question == q)
  sk <- searchk %>% filter(question == q)
  fr <- fit_rows %>% filter(question == q, model == "stm, Spectral start")
  cc <- corpus_counts %>% filter(question == q, scope == "three studies pooled")
  st <- stability %>% filter(question == q) %>% arrange(desc(mean_best_match_correlation))
  av <- avg_change %>% filter(question == q, quantity == "averaged over levels")
  ch <- avg_change %>% filter(question == q, quantity == "Dramatic minus None")
  lv <- by_level %>% filter(question == q)
  converged <- isTRUE(fr$converged)
  dc <- dropped_by_cell %>% filter(question == q, scope == "three studies pooled")
  share_dropped <- function(src, lev) dc$share_dropped[dc$source == src & dc$modification == lev]
  cat(sprintf("**%s (%s).** ", QUESTION_LABELS[[q]], ROLE[[q]]))
  cat(sprintf(paste(
    "Of %s analysed responses, %s kept at least one word and were modelled; %s were",
    "dropped for having none. At None, %s percent of the AI arm's analysed responses",
    "and %s percent of the Human arm's were dropped; at Dramatic, %s and %s percent. "),
    n_(cc$analysed_responses), n_(cc$modelled_responses), n_(cc$dropped_no_counted_word),
    pct(share_dropped("AI", "None")), pct(share_dropped("Human", "None")),
    pct(share_dropped("AI", "Dramatic")), pct(share_dropped("Human", "Dramatic"))))
  cat(sprintf(paste(
    "A modelled response held %s words on average, from a",
    "vocabulary of %s. Over K = %d to %d the held-out likelihood ranged from %s to %s,",
    "%s. It was highest at K = %d (%s), and next",
    "highest at K = %d (%s). The searchK fit at K = %d %s. The model at K = %d %s",
    "%s %d iterations. "),
    formatC(cc$mean_words_per_modelled_response, format = "f", digits = 2),
    n_(cc$vocabulary_size), min(K_RANGE), max(K_RANGE),
    f4(min(sk$heldout_likelihood)), f4(max(sk$heldout_likelihood)),
    trend_text(sk$heldout_likelihood[order(sk$K)]),
    ck$chosen_K, f4(ck$heldout_likelihood_chosen), ck$runner_up_K,
    f4(ck$heldout_likelihood_runner_up), ck$chosen_K,
    if (sk$reached_iteration_limit[sk$K == ck$chosen_K]) "reached the limit of 500 iterations"
    else "settled before the limit",
    ck$chosen_K, if (converged) "converged" else "did not converge",
    if (converged) "after" else "within", fr$em_iterations))
  cat(sprintf(paste(
    "Against the %d refits from the LDA start, the mean best-match correlation of a",
    "topic ranged from %s (topic %d) to %s (topic %d), with a median of %s over the",
    "%d topics. "),
    length(STABILITY_SEEDS), f3(min(st$mean_best_match_correlation)), st$topic[nrow(st)],
    f3(max(st$mean_best_match_correlation)), st$topic[1],
    f3(median(st$mean_best_match_correlation)), nrow(st)))
  big_av <- av[which.max(abs(av$estimate)), ]
  big_ch <- ch[which.max(abs(ch$estimate)), ]
  if (converged) {
    cat(sprintf(paste(
      "Averaged over levels, %d of %d topics have a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value",
      "below .05 for the AI minus Human difference, and %d of %d for its change from None",
      "to Dramatic. Of the %d differences at single levels, %d have a 95 percent interval",
      "that excludes zero, with no adjustment. The largest averaged difference is that of",
      "topic %d (%s): %s percentage points of expected share (95 percent interval %s to",
      "%s; adjusted p %s). The largest change from None to Dramatic is that of topic %d",
      "(%s): %s percentage points (95 percent interval %s to %s; adjusted p %s), with an",
      "AI minus Human difference of %s points at None, %s at Slight and %s at Dramatic."),
      sum(av$p_bh < ALPHA), nrow(av), sum(ch$p_bh < ALPHA), nrow(ch),
      nrow(lv), sum(lv$ci95_lo > 0 | lv$ci95_hi < 0),
      big_av$topic, words_of(q, big_av$topic), pct(big_av$estimate), pct(big_av$ci95_lo),
      pct(big_av$ci95_hi), p_text(big_av$p_bh),
      big_ch$topic, words_of(q, big_ch$topic), pct(big_ch$estimate), pct(big_ch$ci95_lo),
      pct(big_ch$ci95_hi), p_text(big_ch$p_bh),
      pct(lv$estimate[lv$topic == big_ch$topic & lv$level == "None"]),
      pct(lv$estimate[lv$topic == big_ch$topic & lv$level == "Slight"]),
      pct(lv$estimate[lv$topic == big_ch$topic & lv$level == "Dramatic"])))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(paste(
      "Because the model did not converge, its label effects carry no interval or",
      "p-value and are description only. The largest averaged AI minus Human difference",
      "is that of topic %d (%s), %s percentage points of expected share, and the largest",
      "change from None to Dramatic that of topic %d (%s), %s points."),
      big_av$topic, words_of(q, big_av$topic), pct(big_av$estimate),
      big_ch$topic, words_of(q, big_ch$topic), pct(big_ch$estimate)))
  }
  cat("\n\n")
}
cat(paste(
  "Four things limit what these numbers say. The justifications were written after",
  "the ratings, so they describe what people wrote once their number was chosen. The",
  "model reads only the responses that kept a word, and at None the two arms lost",
  "different shares of their responses, so a difference at None compares responses",
  "selected differently in the two arms. The",
  "model treats each response as independent of the others by the same writer, so",
  "its intervals are likely too narrow and the count of intervals that exclude zero",
  "is likely too high. And a topic that the LDA refits do not recover depends on where",
  "the search started as well as on the data, so a label effect on such a topic may",
  "not survive another start. Nothing here tests a registered hypothesis or changes a",
  "registered verdict.\n\n"))
```

# The manifest lists every output this run registered, whether this run
# wrote it, and its SHA-256 checksum. It is written last, and then written
# again with the analysis status as its last column; it does not list itself,
# so the second write changes no checksum in it.
manifest <- write_run_manifest(run)
stopifnot(all(manifest$written_this_run))
write_table(manifest, basename(run$manifest_path))
progress("Run complete; manifest written")
